blocks.markdown: Sift labels new Gmail by importance on a schedule, and reads this doc in full before every run. It's my definition of what matters. Every rule above "Added by sift" is mine, and sift never changes those. Keep it under about two pages.

- **Change a rule:** edit any section above "Added by sift". Sift never changes those.
- **Correct sift:** add or edit a rule here; the next run follows it. Fixing one thread's label or Important mark in Gmail fixes that thread only, and sift won't undo it.
- **Let sift learn on its own:** once a day, sift checks how I handled the mail it labeled. When I reply to or star several threads from one sender that it ranked low, or archive its Important mail unread, it adds a rule starting with "(observed)" under Added by sift.
- **Answer a question:** sift asks in comments that start with "Sift:". Reply in the thread, and the next run applies your answer.
- **Choose newsletters:** list the ones I want to read under Newsletters, Valued. Every other newsletter gets AI/Bulk. Sift adds lines there too, each starting with "(learned)", from its daily check.
- **Choose tabs:** say under Tabs which mail goes in Social, Promotions, or Updates. Sift moves mail to match, whatever tab Gmail picked, and keeps a tab I set by hand.
- **Allow more than labels:** add it under Permissions, for example "Archive threads labeled AI/Junk".
- **Tell sift about yourself:** add notes under About me, grouped by topic. Sift adds its own notes there too, each starting with "(inferred)". Edit one to correct it, or remove "(inferred)" to make it yours.

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Important (Gmail's mark) | I'd want to see it today |
| AI/Low priority | Meant for me, nothing urgent |
| AI/Bulk | Mass mail I wouldn't miss if it were archived unread |
| AI/Junk | Mail I never want |
| Star | Someone is waiting on me |

Who I am, the people in my mail, and what matters to me right now, grouped by topic so related notes sit together. Sift reads this before every run. Lines I write are mine. Sift adds lines that start with "(inferred)", with where it learned each one and when, and it edits only those lines. To keep related notes together, sift may move any line here, mine included, but never changes my words.
### (topic, such as Kids' soccer, Home, or Work)
Senders, topics, or situations that should always be marked Important.

- Anything from a person I have written to in the last 90 days, unless it is clearly bulk mail
- Deadlines, payments, or schedule changes affecting the next 7 days
- Anything from my kids' coaches or teachers
What counts as someone waiting on me specifically, which sift stars. It depends on the message, not on who sent it.

- A direct question addressed to me by name or as the only recipient
- Requests for a decision, approval, or volunteer sign-up
- A statement addressed to me that needs me to acknowledge it, such as a confirmation someone is waiting on
Not a reply, even from someone I know:

- A message to a group that only shares information, such as a note to all tenants about a visit
- An acknowledgment of my own message, such as "ok, thanks" or "got it"
Mail meant for me that doesn't meet the rules above, including:

- Automated notifications that only confirm something already done
- Group threads where I am Cc'd and nothing is asked of me
- Newsletters on my Valued list
- Receipts and statements
- FYIs from people I know
Mass mail I wouldn't miss if it were archived unread, including:

- Newsletters not on my Valued list
- Promotions from companies I've signed up with or bought from
- Social network notifications
Valued newsletters get AI/Low priority. Every other newsletter, listed under Not valued or not listed at all, gets AI/Bulk. One per line: name | sender.

- Promotions and marketing I didn't ask for, even when worded urgently
- Spam-like or phishing-like messages
Labels sift adds alongside the priority label, judged on what a message is, not on the words it happens to use. Sift creates each one under AI/.

- **Receipts, statements, and invoices:** label a message AI/Receipt, AI/Statement, or AI/Invoice when it is one, or carries one as an attachment. A message that only talks about one, such as "where is my receipt for Thursday?" or "I never got an invoice in the mail", gets none of these labels.
- **Newsletters:** label a message AI/Newsletter when it works as a newsletter, whatever it calls itself: a "newsletter", a "gazette", or a regular Friday update that reads like one.
- **Travel:** label AI/Travel the booking confirmations, itineraries, boarding passes, and check-in reminders for trips I've booked. Travel deals and "where to next?" marketing don't count.
- **Deliveries:** label AI/Delivery the tracking updates, "out for delivery", and "delivered" notices for orders I've placed. Shipping promotions don't count.
- **Appointments:** label AI/Appointment the confirmations, reminders, and reschedules for appointments I have, such as a doctor, dentist, or car service. "Book your next visit" promotions don't count.
- **Account security:** label AI/Security the sign-in alerts, password resets, and verification codes from services I use. A message that only looks like one, from a lookalike sender, is Junk instead.

Which Gmail inbox tab each kind of mail belongs in, whatever tab Gmail chose. Sift files every thread it labels here, judged on what the message is, apart from its priority. Important mail always goes to Primary, and so does anything not listed below.
- Notifications from social networks and fitness or community apps
- Marketing, sales, and newsletters from stores and brands

- Receipts, statements, invoices, and bills
- Delivery, travel, and appointment notices
- Account and security alerts
- Automated notifications that only confirm something already done
- Newsletters from clubs and groups I belong to

Rules sift learned from my answers to its questions, and "(observed)" rules from its daily check of how I handle mail. Sift adds, sharpens, and consolidates rules only here. A rule here can narrow one of mine for the cases it names.

Actions beyond priority labels that sift may take, by category. Empty means priority labels only. For example: "Archive threads labeled AI/Junk", or "Label event invitations as invitation". Sift creates any label I name here under AI/ in title case (AI/Invitation).
Real cases that teach the rules. Format: sender | subject | correct label | why.
Newest first. Date | change | prompted by.
What sift did on each run, newest first, so I can check any call. To correct sift, edit the rubric (see its "How to use this doc").
Each run adds its date, time, and start in epoch seconds, a short summary, then one line per thread:
time | thread id | sender | subject | applied | reason
The first run each day also adds a "Daily review" line, and an "observed" line for each sign of how I handled a thread sift labeled.
Times are in the timezone the rubric names.
Run {{date:2026-10-09}} 07:00: processed 0. Daily review: {{date:2026-10-09}}, 0 threads checked, 0 signals.
Runs older than 30 days, rolled up to one line per week.
